title: Ghost hunters spent night in one of Wales' most haunted - what happened next
excerpt: Visitors reported groans, footsteps and mysterious voices during a paranormal investigation at Scolton Manor, Pembrokeshire, this weekend.
content:
For most people, a visit to Scolton Manor involves a stroll around the historic house and grounds.

But for one group at the weekend, the plan was slightly different: switch off the lights, wander around the manor after dark and see if anything decided to wander back.

The event, hosted by paranormal investigator Rachel Hughes of Rachel's Raven Paranormal Events UK, drew 19 visitors keen to experience the historic Pembrokeshire mansion at its creepiest.

Visitors were armed with ghost-hunting gadgets and recording equipment to see them through the six hours of ghost hunting.

And according to those taking part, the manor did not disappoint.

Among the highlights of the evening was the sound of a man's groan on the main staircase (Image: Rachel Hughes)

According to Rachel, one of the highlights of the evening was the sound of a man's groan on the main staircase, heard not once but twice.

There were also reports of footsteps echoing through the building when nobody seemed to be around.

"Several K2 meters lit up in unexpected locations despite there being no obvious electricity sources nearby," she said.

Then came the spirit box sessions, which produced some particularly curious moments.

According to Rachel, guests reported hearing names being called, the sound of a man laughing and what appeared to be references to servants and children discussing hunting rabbits.

Visitors reported groans, footsteps and mysterious voices during a paranormal investigation at Scolton Manor this weekend. (Image: Rachel Hughes)

"We had an interesting night," said Rachel.

"There were lots of bits and bobs, but sometimes it was quiet. However, everyone enjoyed the experience ."

Like any good paranormal investigator, she's not rushing to conclusions.

A camera was left recording in one of the rooms overnight and audio recordings are still being reviewed to see whether anything was captured that might have escaped notice at the time.

Whether that's evidence of spirits, old floorboards doing what old floorboards do best, or something else entirely remains to be seen.

Over the years, staff, visitors and paranormal groups have shared tales of unexplained footsteps in Scolton Manor. (Image: Rachel Hughes)

The reports certainly fit with Scolton Manor's longstanding spooky reputation.

Over the years, staff, visitors and paranormal groups have shared tales of unexplained footsteps, voices from empty rooms and shadowy figures moving through the house.

One previous investigation even singled out the kitchen as a hotspot for unusual activity.

To its credit, Scolton Manor takes a refreshingly balanced approach to ghost-hunting. While acknowledging the strange experiences many people report, the attraction is quick to point out that there are often perfectly natural explanations.

"Experiences are personal and there can be perfectly natural explanations for many things that happen during an investigation," said a spokesperson for Scolton Manor.

"That's exactly why we love doing them.

"You investigate, you record, you question it - and you make your own mind up."

As for this weekend's visitors, they left with plenty of stories to tell.

Whether the group encountered resident spirits, echoes of the manor's past or simply the quirks of a centuries-old building is open to debate.

For those tempted to swap a normal night out for a ghost hunt, bookings for Rachel's Raven Paranormal Events UK are available via Facebook.
